hook: A Pico 2 W dreams up games with a tiny transformer.
hooks: A Pico 2 W dreams up games with a tiny transformer.
It uses two tiny neural nets to generate frames and choose actions.
SheepSeb says the world model uses 26k–131k parameters.
what_happened: A looped transformer generates game frames and a small MLP picks actions, both running on a Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W.
try_it: Play the real game in a terminal with `uv run python -m tinyworldformer.games.play --game pacman`; flashing a Pico uses ./flash.sh.
why_it_matters: On the chip, the actor only sees frames from the world model and never touches the real game.
the_catch: The author says the frame rate has not been measured on the Pico itself yet.
caption: A tiny looped transformer can generate and play games directly on a Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W. Can your microcontroller dream up games?
alt_text: The slides explain that a Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W runs a tiny looped transformer that generates simple games and a small network that plays them, how to try it, and a limitation.

es.hook: Un Pico 2 W imagina juegos con un pequeño transformer.
es.what_happened: Un transformer en bucle genera fotogramas del juego y una pequeña MLP selecciona acciones; ambos se ejecutan en una Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W.
es.try_it: Juega al juego real en una terminal con `uv run python -m tinyworldformer.games.play --game pacman`; para flashear el Pico usa ./flash.sh.
es.why_it_matters: En el chip, el agente solo ve fotogramas del modelo del mundo y nunca interactúa con el juego real.
es.the_catch: El autor dice que la tasa de fotogramas aún no se ha medido en el propio Pico.
